{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Greece|Cuisine of Greece]] | [[Cookbook:Appetizers|Appetizers]]

'''Saganaki''' is a Greek or Greek-American dish consisting of a [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|hard, white, brined cheese]] cooked simply with olive oil in a hot pan (traditionally a two-handed vessel whence the name of the dish), usually served with [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]. In American restaurants, it is sometimes flambeed with various liqueurs at the table. In Greece, it is a traditional dish to have both with liquor (as a [[wikipedia:meze|meze]]) or at the beginning of the meal to whet the appetite. 

==Ingredients==
*1 large slice of salty, brined white [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]] (e.g. [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta]], sirene)
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] (''not'' extra virgin)
*1 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] wedge
*A small amount of [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] (optional)
*[[Cookbook:Bread|Pita or other bread]] (optional) 

==Procedure==
#Heat a small [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] over medium-high heat.
#While the pan heats, cut the cheese into slices of the desired size and thickness. Thicker slices will take longer to melt through and may result in burning, while thinner ones will have less chance to brown. 
#Optionally, dredge the slices in flour—this will create a darker and slightly crispier crust, but is an optional step as the cheese will acquire a very slight crust on its own by virtue of the oil and high heat. It will also reduce the spitting somewhat.
#Add the oil to the hot pan and swirl it around. When the oil shimmers and seems to become more fluid, it is ready. Add the cheese and step back—it will spit due to the brine-water on the cheese.
#Flip the cheese after a minute or two. A slice of ¾ centimeter should get about 1–2 minutes per side.
#Serve immediately, with lemon and (optionally) bread.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The best and most traditional cheese to use is [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta]], kefalograviera, kasseri, or kefalotyri.
